title: A fresh second projection closes an already committed request
question: What happens when an exact effect is present, the primary projection is stale and the second is fresh?
limit: One authored review-metadata case with an exact prior effect and a non-deduplicating receiver. It illustrates a condition, not the frequency of that condition.

title: Both receiver projections unavailable
question: Does a gateway close the case if neither status source is reachable?
limit: One authored review-metadata case begins with an exact effect. The workflows cannot verify it from the two unavailable projections.

title: A successful verifier lookup returns stale approval
question: Which route follows when the index responds successfully with a stale revision?
limit: One release-check decision at logical tick 1. The fixture supplies the current revision. Both arms use the same expected decision and observations.

title: Verifier fallback expiry across the process boundary
question: Does the serving check keep using a verifier fallback after its validity window ends?
limit: One serving-check decision at logical tick 3 in same-owner local processes. The comparison does not include authorization and use racing in production.

title: Extracted routine verifies within an expanded-work cap
question: Can the whole-program arm and the extracted-routine arm finish the same task within the same expanded-work cap?
limit: One authored board-routing case with a descriptive query and forward order. Exhaustion leaves solvability open.

title: The same whole program under two queue priorities
question: Can changing only the queue priority remove a verified result within the same proposal cap?
limit: One authored b24 board-routing case. Both arms have the same descriptive query and 96-proposal cap. This case illustrates scheduler sensitivity, independently of claims about other programs.

title: An earlier authorized write observed after revocation
question: What does the journal show about a write that precedes revocation and is observed later?
limit: One schedule in a same-owner local database. A later observation does not change the grant that was in force when the effect committed.

title: A second reading corrects the scientific verdict
question: When does a context disagreement hide a justified contradiction?
limit: One held-out claim. Pooling included annotated sentence 4 alongside sentence 0. The exact-rationale criterion gives that extra sentence no precision credit.

title: The citation veto withholds an unsupported verdict
question: Can the veto prevent an unsupported contradiction?
limit: One held-out claim with no annotated evidence in the selected abstract. The result uses the frozen rationale scoring rule.

title: Two readings agree on an unsupported verdict
question: Can both readings accept the same unsupported citation?
limit: One held-out claim with no annotated rationale in the retrieved paper. Agreement within one model shares its failure modes.
